questions.question: A takes 10 days more than B to finish a task. They both do the work together for 5 days and finish (8)/({15)} part of the work. How long will B alone take to complete the whole work?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

A takes 10 days more than B to finish a task.

They both do the work together for 5 days and finish part of the work.

**Concept used:**

The time is taken by A to complete the work = a

The time is taken by B to complete the work = b

The amount of work done = L.C.M of (a and b) = c

Efficiency of A = (c)/(a)

Efficiency of B = (c)/(b)

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

Let the time taken by B to complete the work = x days

The time taken by A to complete the work = x + 10 days

The amount of work done = (x)(x + 10)

Efficiency of A = ((x)(x+10))/(x+10) = x units a day

Efficiency of B = ((x)(x+10))/(x) = (x + 10) units a day

Now, 

The amount of work done by A in 5 days = 5x

The amount of work done by B in 5 days = 5(x + 10) = 5x + 50

The total amount of work done in 5 days = 5x + 5x + 50 = 10x + 50

Again according to the question,

⇒ 10x + 50 = (8)/({15)} of (x)(x + 10)

Now by using the value of option.

Option A: x = 15

⇒ 10(15) + 50 = (8)/({15)} of (15)(15 + 10)

⇒ 150 + 50 = 8 × 25

⇒ 200 = 200

Therefore, the time is taken by B to complete the work = 15 days

**Therefore, '15 days' is the required answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**

A takes 10 days more than B to finish a task.

They both do the work together for 5 days and finish (8)/({15)} part of the work. 

⇒ 8over15(Total work) = 5 Days 

⇒ Total work = 15×5over 8 Days

⇒ Total work = 75/8 Days ..... (1)

Now we will help from the option,

Option (1) - B = 15 Days

⇒ A = 15 + 10 = 25 Days

questions.question: A train covers a distance of 14 km in 10 min. If its speed is decreased by 4 km/h, then how much time will be taken by it to cover the same distance?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A train covers a distance of 14 km in 10 min. 

Its speed is decreased by 4 km/h in the second case.

**Concept used:**

Speed = (distance)/(time)

**Calculation:**

The time taken by the train to cover 14 km = 10 min = (10)/(60) hour

The speed of train = (14)/(frac{10){60}} = 84 kmph

The decreased speed = 84 - 4 = 80 kmph

The time taken by the train to cover the same distance = (14)/(80) × 60 = 10(1)/(2) min

**∴ 10(1)/(2) min is the required answer.**

questions.question: The ratio of acid and water in solution A is 1 ∶ 5 and that in solution B is 2 ∶ 7. If equal quantities of both the solutions are mixed, then what will be the ratio of acid and water in the new solution?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of acid and water in solution A is 1 ∶ 5 and that in solution B is 2 ∶ 7.

Equal quantities of both solutions are mixed

**Calculation:**

In solution A:

The amount of acid = 1 unit

The amount of water = 5 units

The total unit of acid and water in solution A = 6 units

In solution B:

The amount of acid = 2 unit

The amount of water = 7 units

The total unit of acid and water in solution A = 9 units

∵ The quantity of both solutions are mixed in equal quantity 

∴ Multiply the ratio of acid and water in solution A by 9 and multiply the ratio of acid and water in solution B by 6.

The ratio of acid and water in solution A = 9 ∶ 45 

The ratio of acid and water in solution B = 12 ∶ 42

The total quantity of acid in the final solution,

⇒ 9 + 12 = 21 units

The total quantity of water in the final solution,

⇒ 45 + 42 = 87 units

The required ratio of acid and water = 21 : 87 = 7 : 29

**Hence, '7 : 29' is the required answer.**

questions.question: Ravina saves 16(2)/(3)% of her monthly income. When her monthly expenses increase by 10% (income remains the same), she is able to save Rs. 1,275 a month. Her monthly income (in Rs.) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ravina saves 16(2)/(3)% of her monthly income.

When her monthly expenses increase by 10% (income remains the same), she is able to save Rs. 1,275 a month.

**Calculation:**

Let x be the monthly income of Ravina.

The amount Ravina saves = 16(2)/(3)% of x = (x)/(6)

The monthly expenses of Ravina = x - (x)/(6) = (5x)/(6)

According to the question,

The increased monthly expenses = (100% + 10%) of (5x)/(6) = (5.5x)/(6)

The amount Ravina saves = x - (5.5x)/(6) = (0.5x)/(6)

Now,

⇒ (0.5x)/(6) = 1275

⇒ x = Rs. 15300

**∴ 'Rs. 15300' is the required answer.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Ravina saves 1/6th of the monthly income,

Thus, if Income = 6a then, savings = a 

Then expenditure = 6a - a = 5a

When expenditure increases by 10%, 

New expenditure = 5a × 110/100

⇒ 5.5a

Now, new savings = 6a - 5.5a 

0.5a, which is equal to Rs. 1275.

⇒ a = 2550

Monthly income = 6a

⇒ 6 × 2550 = 15300.

**Hence, the correct answer is Rs. 15300**

questions.solution:

Second Discount = 10%

Marked price = Rs. 500

**Concept used:**

Overall discount,

Dₒ = D₁ + D₂ - (D₁ × D₂)/(100)

Where, D₁ = First discount, D₂ = Second discount, 

Dₒ = Overall discount

Selling price = (100% - Discoun%) × Marked Price

**Calculation used:**

According to the question,

⇒ Do = 30 + 10 - (30 × 10)/(100)

⇒ Do = 40 - 3 = 37%

The selling price of the pen = (100% - 37%) of 500 = Rs. 315

**Therefore, 'Rs. 315' is the required answer.**

questions.question: The cost price of one toy is Rs. 375. A shopkeeper sells 12 toys at a profit of 20% and 8 toys at a loss of 10%. Had he sold all the 20 toys at 9% profit, then his increased in profit would have:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The cost price of one toy is Rs. 375.

In the first case:

A shopkeeper sells 12 toys at a profit of 20% and 8 toys at a loss of 10%. 

In the second case:

Had he sold all the 20 toys at 9% profit, 

**Concept used:**

Selling price = (100% + Profit%) of Cost price

Selling price = (100% - Loss%) of Cost price

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

In the first case:

The selling price of the toy for selling it at 20% profit = (100% + 20%) of 375 = Rs. 450

The total price of selling 12 toys = 450 × 12 = Rs. 5400

The selling price of the toy for selling it at 10% loss = (100% - 10%) of 375 = Rs. 337.5

The total selling price of 8 toys = 337.5 × 8 = Rs. 2700

Therefore, the total selling price of 20 toys = Rs. 5400 + Rs. 2700 = Rs. 8100

The cost price of 20 toys = Rs. 375 × 20 = Rs. 7500

The net profit = Rs. 8100 - Rs. 7500 = Rs. 600

In the second case:

The selling price of one toy at 9% profit = (100% + 9%) of Rs. 375 = Rs. 408.75

The selling price of all 20 toys = Rs. 408.75 × 20 = Rs. 8175

The net profit = Rs. 8175 - Rs. 7500 = Rs. 675

The net increase in profit = Rs. 675 - Rs. 600 = Rs. 75

**Therefore, '**increased by Rs. 75**' is the required answer.**

questions.question: A can complete 60% of a work in 6 days and B can complete the same work in 15 days. They work together for 3 days. The remaining work is completed by C alone in 12 days. In how many days will C alone complete (1)/({8)} part of the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can complete 60% of a work in 6 days and B can complete the same work in 15 days. 

They work together for 3 days. 

The remaining work is completed by C alone in 12 days.

Concept used:

The time is taken by A to complete the work = a

The time is taken by B to complete the work = b

The amount of work done = L.C.M of (a and b) = c

Efficiency of A = (c)/(a)

Efficiency of B = (c)/(b)

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

The time is taken by A to complete 60% of the work = 6 days

The time is taken by A to complete 100% of the work = (6)/(60) × 100 = 10 days

The time is taken by B to complete the work = 15 days

The total unit of work = L.C.M of (10 and 15) = 30 units

Efficiency of A = (30)/(10) = 3 units a day

Efficiency of B = (30)/(15) = 2 units a day

Now,

The amount of work done by A in 3 days = 3 × 3 = 9 units

The amount of work done by B in 3 days = 2 × 3 = 6 units

The total amount of work by A and B in 3 days = 9 + 6 = 15 units

The remaining amount of work = 30 - 15 = 15 units

The time is taken by C to complete the remaining work = 12 days

Efficiency of C = (15)/(12) = 1.25 units a day

Again according to the question,

The time is taken by C to complete the (1)/(8) of work = (frac{30)/(8)}{1.25} = 3 days

**Therefore, '3 days' is the required answer.**

questions.question: If the average of the squares of two consecutive odd natural numbers is 145, then the average of the two numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the average of the two consecutive odd numbers be A.

The numbers can be written as (A − 1) and (A + 1).

Average of their squares = [(A − 1)² + (A + 1)²] ÷ 2 = (2A² + 2) ÷ 2 = A² + 1

Given, A² + 1 = 145 ⇒ A² = 144 ⇒ A = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The average of the squares of two consecutive odd natural numbers is 145.

**Calculations:**

Let the two consecutive odd natural numbers be n and n + 2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b13ae9bdbaebe99a30065559567c38d525978884377a95830d36857022537c34.png] 

⇒ Average of their squares = [n² + (n + 2)²] ÷ 2 = 145

⇒ n² + n² + 4n + 4 = 145 × 2

⇒ 2n² + 4n + 4 = 290

⇒ 2n² + 4n − 286 = 0

Dividing the equation by 2:

⇒ n² + 2n − 143 = 0

⇒ n² + 13n − 11n − 143 = 0

⇒ n(n + 13) − 11(n + 13) = 0

⇒ (n − 11)(n + 13) = 0

Since n is a natural number, n cannot be negative. Hence, n = 11.

The two numbers are 11 and (11 + 2) = 13.

Average of the numbers = (11 + 13) ÷ 2 = 12.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Consecutive Odd Numbers

Consecutive odd numbers always have a difference of 2. They can be generally represented as 2k − 1 and 2k + 1, where k is a natural number.

Algebraic Identity for Squares

The sum of squares of (A − B) and (A + B) simplifies calculations directly: (A − B)² + (A + B)² = 2(A² + B²).

Average of Consecutive Numbers

The arithmetic mean or average of any two consecutive odd numbers is strictly the even number present exactly between them.

**Concept used:**

(1.) Area of triangle = √(s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c))

(2.) Semi-perimeter, s = (a+b+c)/(2)

Where, 

a, b and c are the lengths of the three sides of the triangle.

(3.) Area of square = x²

Where, 

x is the side length of the square

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

⇒ s = (60+297+303)/(2)

⇒ s = 330 m

Now,

⇒ A = √(330(330 - 60)(330 - 297)(330 - 303))

⇒ A = √(330 × 270 × 33 × 27)

⇒ A = 8910 m²

Again according to the question,

⇒ Area of square, x² = 8910

⇒ x = 9√110

The perimeter of square = 4x = 36√110 m

**Therefore, '**36√110 m**' is the required answer.**
